tasks.title: Build the persistent engineering control plane
tasks.rationale: Project state lived in prose documents and an agent transcript. Nothing detected a new repository, a moved HEAD or a changed file, and nothing could answer 'what is integrated and what is proven' from the filesystem. This cycle creates typed manifests, a Rust scanner/validator, idempotent task generation and an evidence report.
acceptance_criteria: Manifests exist for repositories, modules, agents, interfaces, capabilities, dependencies, tasks and quality, and validate cross-references.
A workspace scan observes Git state, file digests and Cargo packages without modifying any source repository.
A changed file is reported with its path; a missing declared repository and a HEAD past the verified commit are reported.
Running an unchanged scan twice produces no changes and no duplicate tasks.
Task ids are derived from the observed value, and cycle detection names only the tasks in the cycle.
A report is generated from the manifests with counts that match the files.
required_tests: cargo test -p cad-engineering
zentrion-eng validate
zentrion-eng scan --write twice
evidence: zentrion-eng validate: 0 errors, 4 warnings (unrecorded dependency licences)
two consecutive scans: 0 changes, backlog SHA-256 unchanged
tasks.rollback: The cycle adds one workspace member and a new engineering/ tree. Removing the member and the directories restores the prior state; no source repository was modified.

tasks.title: Connect the contract and the truck adapter to a real consumer
tasks.rationale: The contract and the adapter had no consumer other than their own tests, so 'integrated' was a claim about files rather than about use. A headless CLI now converts units, writes a versioned document header, builds geometry through the adapter, tessellates, and writes a binary STL that an independent parser reads back correctly.
acceptance_criteria: A unit-aware request produces a document header whose units and tolerance match the request.
Volumes are analytic: a 10x10x5 mm box is 500 mm3 and a documented union fixture is 1120 mm3.
The mesh crossing the boundary is watertight and consistently oriented.
The written STL is valid binary STL and round-trips through an independent parser.
No capability is advertised that a test does not exercise.
required_tests: cargo test -p cad-cli
cargo test -p cad-kernel-truck
evidence: independent binary-STL parse: box 12 triangles, 500.0000 mm3, 0 open edges; union 82 triangles, 1120.0037 mm3, 0 open edges
tasks.rollback: Removing crates/cad-cli from the workspace members and deleting the directory restores the previous state; the adapter change is independent and documented in ADR-0005.

tasks.title: Implement cancellation and deadlines in the truck adapter
tasks.rationale: KernelError::Cancelled and Timeout exist in the contract but nothing sets them. Without them a UI cannot abandon a long boolean and an agent runtime cannot enforce a budget.
acceptance_criteria: Every kernel entry point accepts a deadline and a cancellation token.
Exceeding the deadline returns Timeout and leaves the kernel state usable.
A test cancels a long operation and then performs a successful operation on the same instance.
required_tests: cargo test -p cad-kernel-truck
evidence: crates/cad-kernel-truck/src/lib.rs: Budget, CancellationToken, Deadline and the _with_budget twins on every operation
tasks.rollback: The API change is additive if the existing methods delegate with an unlimited deadline.

tasks.title: Build an analytic boolean correctness corpus
tasks.rationale: The difference defect and the third-union panic were both found by accident. A fixture set with analytic volumes turns them into a regression gate and gives an honest per-kernel reliability comparison instead of README claims.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures cover coplanar cut, piercing cut, contained void, tangent contact, near-degenerate sliver, thin wall, coordinates near 1e6 mm, and a non-axis-aligned box.
Each fixture asserts analytic volume and area with a stated tolerance.
A table prints pass/fail per kernel and exits non-zero if a previously passing case regresses.
Boolean difference is recorded as unsupported until it passes, not silently skipped.
required_tests: cargo test -p cad-kernel-truck
the corpus binary exits non-zero on a wrong volume
evidence: crates/cad-kernel-truck/src/corpus.rs: 10 analytic fixtures, each with a stated volume and area tolerance
crates/cad-kernel-truck/examples/corpus.rs: the table, exiting non-zero on a regression

Measured table: box_control, non_axis_aligned_box, union_partial_overlap, intersection_thin_wall and intersection_near_degenerate_sliver pass; union_tangent_contact and intersection_large_coordinates are recorded known failures; the three difference fixtures are recorded unsupported, not skipped.
tasks.rollback: The corpus is additive; deleting the example removes it.

tasks.title: Design and implement the CadAgent runtime
tasks.rationale: The brief requires pluggable agents, but no trait, registry, permission check, lifecycle enforcement or scheduling exists. Registering an agent before that would be a claim without an implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned CadAgent contract exists with metadata, capabilities, schemas, context, budgets and structured errors.
A registry enforces the discovered-to-registered-to-ready lifecycle and refuses to activate an agent whose contract tests have not passed.
Permissions are capability-based; filesystem, network and shell access are denied unless declared, and shell/secrets require an owner decision.
Contract tests cover an incompatible agent being rejected.
required_tests: cargo test -p cad-agent-runtime
evidence: crates/cad-agent-api/src/agent.rs, contract.rs, permission.rs, error.rs: the versioned contract
crates/cad-agent-runtime/src/registry.rs: the lifecycle, grants, budgets and quarantine
crates/cad-agent-runtime/src/schema.rs: the strict JSON Schema subset checker
tasks.rollback: New crates only; removing them from workspace members restores the previous state.

tasks.title: Implement the geometry-ops agent and run it through the registry
tasks.rationale: The agent runtime existed but nothing exercised it: there was a trait, a registry, a schema checker and a permission model, and no agent a caller could run. The first real agent also has to prove that the runtime's guarantees hold for an agent that does actual work, rather than only for the registry's own test doubles.
acceptance_criteria: An agent implements the CadAgent trait and is registrable, activatable and runnable in the registry.
The runtime's schema enforcement refuses a hostile input before the agent sees it.
The agent's effective grant decides whether its file-reading operation runs; without the grant it is refused and every other operation still works.
A call cancelled by the caller returns Cancelled, and the agent is usable for the next call.
A call that outlives its wall-clock budget returns Timeout.
The output and call budgets are enforced by the registry, not by the agent.
Every reply satisfies the contract's declared output schema.
required_tests: cargo test -p cad-agent-geometry
evidence: engineering/quality/tests.json#t-cad-agent-runtime (16 passed: the upper-bound keywords maxItems, maximum and maxLength were added for this agent's contract)
tasks.rollback: Remove crates/cad-agent-geometry from the workspace members and the repository, module, capability, interface, dependency and agent entries from the manifests. The only other change is three added schema keywords in cad-agent-runtime, which are additive and independently tested.

`Kernel::revolve(&self, profile, axis_origin, axis_direction, angle_radians) -> Result<SolidId, KernelError>` added with an `Unsupported` default, so no adapter that cannot revolve has to change.
Revolution is full-turn only at this layer: an angle that is not a full turn is `KernelError::Invalid` with a reason.

Volumes are measured from a tessellated mesh, so a revolve reads a fraction of a percent low (inscribed polygon); the tests bound that with the chord tolerance rather than claiming exactness.
A revolve can only start, join or cut the single running body; it cannot pattern, mirror or produce a second body.
The revolve is not benchmarked: no performance record exists for it, so cost is unmeasured.
Revolve is verified through the API and one scripted browser run; it has not been benchmarked and has not been tried on a profile with more than a handful of points.

tasks.title: Crash-safe recovery for unsaved edits
tasks.rationale: A measured production-readiness check lost an unsaved edit on kill -9: 24,000 mm3 became 12,000 mm3 on reopen, with no snapshot, no warning and no way back. A professional tool may not lose work between saves, and a corrupt project file had no fallback at all. This slice adds a recovery snapshot next to the project, restores it on start when it belongs to the current file version, and lets the user promote or discard it.
acceptance_criteria: An unsaved edit survives an abrupt process death and is offered on the next start.
The recovery snapshot never writes or replaces the project file; saving stays an explicit action.
A snapshot taken from an older version of the file is not offered, and a corrupt snapshot is ignored rather than blocking the project.
When the project file itself cannot be read, a valid snapshot becomes the only copy and the session says so.
The UI shows that a recovered session is unsaved, and offers one action to discard it back to the file.
required_tests: cargo test --offline -p cad-document
cargo test --offline -p cad-studio
cargo test --offline --workspace -j 2
tasks.rollback: Stop writing the snapshot: remove the `save_recovery` call in `StudioState::autosave` and the `recovery` field from the state payload. The document functions are additive and unused by any other caller, and the file format is a separate file, so no project file is ever written by the feature and rollback cannot corrupt a document.
acceptance_results: Met: a real `kill -9` on the release binary after an unsaved 800 mm3 edit reopened at 800 mm3, printed `recovered: unsaved changes from the recovery snapshot`, and reported `recovered: true`, `dirty: true` in `/api/state`. The same flow is a cargo test over a real socket (`an_unsaved_edit_survives_a_crash_and_can_be_saved_or_discarded`).

Met: `save_recovery` writes `<file>.recovery` through the atomic temp+fsync+rename path; the test asserts the project file still holds the pre-edit depth (5 mm) after the crash, and that only an explicit save changes it.

Met: staleness is decided by the file mtime recorded when the snapshot was taken, so a save supersedes the snapshot and the reopened file wins (test: `a_snapshot_superseded_by_a_save_is_deleted_rather_than_offered`); a corrupt snapshot is ignored and the project opens normally (`a_corrupt_snapshot_is_ignored_instead_of_blocking_the_project`).

Met: a truncated project file with a valid snapshot opens the snapshot with `file_unreadable: true`, and the banner says the file could not be read; the discard action is hidden because there is nothing to go back to (`an_unreadable_project_falls_back_to_its_snapshot`).

Met, driven in a browser: the banner reads `Recovered unsaved changes from 10:59 AM…`, the badge reads `unsaved`, the body is the recovered 800 mm3, discard restores the file's 500 mm3 and the `saved` badge, and a later edit does not re-show the recovered banner; zero console errors (9 assertions).
limitations: Named revisions (the rest of M11f) are not implemented: the snapshot is a single last-unsaved-edit file, not a history.
The snapshot is written on every mutation, synchronously; on a very large project that will add a write per edit and has not been measured.
Only one snapshot exists per project, and it is not versioned beyond `RECOVERY_SCHEMA`.
Recovery is per file path: a project opened from a different path does not see the snapshot.
The autosave failure is reported in the payload and the banner, but the edit still succeeds, so a read-only directory leaves the session unprotected until the user notices.
No fsync of the directory entry after the snapshot rename beyond what `atomic_replace` already does for saves.

tasks.title: Release gate, licence policy, SBOM and a verified deployable bundle
tasks.rationale: The production-readiness assessment found no automated gate at all: every quality claim was run by hand, no dependency licence was checked, no SBOM existed, and the only deployable artifact was whatever `cargo build` left in `target/`. A customer or a procurement review cannot rely on that. This slice makes the gate executable in one command, makes the licence policy fail closed on unknown licences, produces a deterministic SBOM, packages and re-verifies a bundle, and drives the real release binary through a live end-to-end simulation including a crash.
acceptance_criteria: One committed command runs fmt, clippy with warnings denied, the workspace tests, the analytic corpus, manifest validation, the licence policy, the SBOM check and the live simulation.
Every dependency's licence is checked against a policy that fails closed: an unrecognised licence is a failure, and banned kernels are refused whatever their licence says.
A deterministic CycloneDX SBOM of the resolved graph is generated offline and contains every package.
A deployable bundle is built, checksummed, archived, extracted into a clean directory and smoke-tested with the packaged binaries.

The live simulation drives the real release server through cut, join, undo/redo, a parameter rebuild, save, restart, STL export and a kill -9 recovery, and loads the built page in a browser when one exists.

./scripts/package.sh
python3 scripts/simulate.py
node scripts/browser-check.mjs <url>
tasks.rollback: Delete the scripts and the `supply` module; no product behaviour depends on them. The SBOM and policy files are generated/declarative artefacts, and the CI workflow is additive. The only source change is the new `atlas-eng licences` and `atlas-eng sbom` subcommands, which no other code calls.
acceptance_results: Met: `./scripts/gate.sh` ran end to end and passed: fmt clean, clippy 0 warnings, 284 tests, corpus 8 ok / 3 known failure / 0 regressions, manifests 0/0, licences 83/83 allowed, SBOM 83 components, simulation 52 assertions (31 HTTP, 21 CLI/control-plane, plus 7 browser). `--quick` skips only the simulation.

Met: `atlas-eng licences` reads the resolved `cargo metadata` offline (host-platform filtered, because resolving every target needs crates that are not cached) and exits 1 on a denied or unknown token. Five unit tests cover legacy slash expressions, parenthesised AND, WITH exceptions, denied-over-allowed and missing licences; banned crates are denied whatever their licence.

Met: `atlas-eng sbom --write` produces `engineering/sbom/atlascad.cdx.json` (CycloneDX 1.5, 83 components, `pkg:cargo/…` purls, licence expressions and the verdict), byte-identical across runs; a test asserts determinism on a fixture.

Met: `./scripts/package.sh` produced `atlas-cad-0.1.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` (3.1 MB), extracted it into a temporary directory, verified `SHA256SUMS`, ran `--help` on all three binaries and built a 10x10x5 STL with the packaged CLI.

Met: `scripts/simulate.py` (52 assertions) starts the release binary, then drives the shipped `atlas` and `atlas-eng` binaries on real files (box and union STL volumes, a 40x30x10 project set to depth 20 and undone, manifest validation, the 83-package licence policy, a byte-identical SBOM and the engineering report); cuts a circle, joins a plate (+11000 mm³ within 0.1), undoes and redoes, rebuilds at a new depth against the measured polygon area, saves, exports and re-parses the STL volume, restarts, then edits without saving, kill -9, restarts and asserts the recovered body before discarding. `scripts/browser-check.mjs` loaded the live page in headless Chrome with zero console errors.
limitations: The GitHub Actions workflow has not been executed on a runner; only the gate it calls was run here.
No code signing, notarisation, installer package or update channel exists; the bundle is a tarball.
Advisory scanning (`cargo-deny`/`cargo-audit`) needs a network and is a CI-only job; it has not run yet.
The simulation requires python3, and the browser check requires Node and Chrome; both degrade with an explicit SKIP message.
The licence policy is a static allow list; a new dependency with a novel permissive licence fails until someone adds it deliberately, which is intended but does add friction.
MPL-2.0 is neither allowed nor denied, so it fails as unknown until a written decision exists.
The bundle is built for the host target only; there is no cross-build matrix.

The arc is the missing entity; the segmented half of the requirement was already met by the drawn polyline, so duplicating it would have added a second spelling of one shape.

Analytic area tests exist for an L-shape and a sector-shaped profile, asserted against the shoelace area.
A cut feature exercises at least one of the new profiles, so the new profile is not untested in the boolean path.

tasks.title: Named revisions and the last-good on-disk copy
tasks.rationale: Crash recovery kept one last-unsaved-edit snapshot, so there was no way to come back to a known-good state after a bad edit, and a corrupt project file with no snapshot was unrecoverable. A user needs a named restore point they can return to by name, and a CAD file needs a previous good copy so a truncated write is not the end of the document.
acceptance_criteria: The document records named, timestamped revisions stored separately from undo, surviving save/reopen.
A revision can be named and recovered by ID, and a restore is reversible.
The last good on-disk revision is retained so a corrupt file with no snapshot is recoverable.
The studio has a revisions panel and a palette command to revert to a named revision.
required_tests: cargo test --offline -p cad-document
cargo test --offline -p cad-studio
cargo test --offline --workspace -j 2
./scripts/gate.sh
tasks.rollback: Drop `revisions`/`next_revision` from the project, `NamedRevision`/`RevisionSummary`, the three revision methods and the three studio routes, and revert `PROJECT_SCHEMA` to 6. A schema-7 file without revisions is a valid schema-6 file apart from the version field; a file with revisions must have them exported first, because the rollback cannot read them. The backup file is independent: stop calling `refresh_backup` and the old file simply stops being retained.
acceptance_results: Met: `Project` persists `revisions` and `next_revision` under schema 7; `a_named_revision_restores_the_history_it_captured` and `revisions_are_named_and_bounded_and_survive_save_and_reopen` cover record, restore, save/reopen and delete. A revision copies parameters/sketches/features only, so it cannot resurrect a deleted copy or a stale undo stack.

Met: names are trimmed, non-empty, at most 80 characters and unique case-insensitively; ids are a separate space; `restore_revision` pushes the current history onto the undo stack first, and the test undoes the restore back to 1200 mm3. Over HTTP an unknown id is 404 unknown_revision.

Met: `save` copies the previous file to `<path>.backup` through a temporary file and a rename; `a_corrupt_project_opens_its_previous_good_copy` truncates the file and opens the 5 mm backup with `source: Backup`, then repairs it by saving. `a_damaged_project_reopens_the_previous_saved_copy` asserts the same over HTTP, including `recovery.source: backup` in /api/state.

Met and browser-driven: the Revisions panel records `browser baseline`, a parameter edit changes the body, Restore returns the original measurement, and the palette offers `Restore revision “browser baseline”` (4 new assertions, 15 loopback + 17 shared, zero console errors).
contract_changes: Studio routes POST /api/revision, /api/revision/restore, /api/revision/remove; `revisions` and `recovery.source` added to the state payload.
limitations: A revision is a full copy of the history, so file size grows with each one; only the 32-copy bound limits it.
No diff, labels, tags, branches, merge or cloud copy.
The palette's save command uses the panel's name field or generates `Revision N`, which is convenient but not descriptive.
The backup is best-effort: a save in a read-only or full directory succeeds without refreshing it.
Snapshot and backup are per file path; opening the same document from another path sees neither.
No audit log of who created a revision (single-user application; there is no account layer).
evidence: scripts/browser-check.mjs (4 new assertions; 15 loopback + 17 shared, 0 console errors)
